guide: Open Start and type your imprint name and your own targets in the yellow cells: yearly return, read-through thresholds, margin, the shared cost rule and the royalties you want each month. Every target is your own number.

Check Titles and Series. Titles holds the facts of each title, the production cost and the expected read-through; Series holds the books you plan. A first-time author with one to three books fills a few rows.

Enter or paste the copies and royalties of each title and month in Sales by Title and Month, and the ad spend and production paid in Costs by Title and Month. Page reads are an estimate that moves every month.
Enter every business expense in Expenses and mark it Shared or a pen name. Shared costs are split between the pen names by the rule you choose on Start.

Read Read-through by Step, Read-through Chain, Where Readers Drop and Value of a Reader: they fill in by themselves from Titles and show where readers leave a series and what a book-1 reader is worth.
Read Pen Profit and Shared Costs by Rule for the profit of each pen name. A small press reads the pen-name columns as author columns.
Read Yearly Return Test, Catalogue Decisions, Title Trend, Title Ranking and Backlist and Frontlist to decide which titles to keep, reprice, repackage or retire.
Use Box Set and Bundle Cases and Target Income Steps to plan a box set or the books needed for the monthly royalties you want.

Use the 18 calculators to judge a series, the price of book 1, a box set, a title or a pen name; print 12 sheets and 12 documents, follow 12 checklists and tap a message link to send a text with the details already written in.
Figures are estimates until the stores pay and every target is your own number; confirm tax and cost split questions with your adviser. No macros, works in Excel and Google Sheets.

listing.title: Author and Self-Publisher Series, Title and Pen-Name Performance Excel Template: Read-through, Reader Value, Pen-Name P&L, Return Test
listing.headline: See which books, series and pen names earn their keep and what to do next
listing.description:
Run the performance side of an author or small publishing business in one Excel workbook. Built for an independent author who publishes under one or two pen names, often with a part-time assistant and freelancers. Series Money Case turns the books you plan, the cost of each, the gap between releases and your own read-through into 24 months of copies, the payback and the book at which to stop. Read-through by Step compares the copies of book n and book n+1 with thresholds you set (read-through is the share of readers of one book who go on to buy the next), and Where Readers Drop ranks every step by readers lost.

Value of a Reader multiplies your royalty per copy by the read-through chain to show what a book-1 buyer is worth over the whole series and the most a sale of book 1 may cost in ads. Pen Profit splits revenue, direct costs and shared costs by the rule you choose (equal, by revenue or by number of titles) and the Shared Cost Rule Comparer shows the swing. Yearly Return Test sets the royalties of the last 12 months against the production cost of each title, and Catalogue Decisions gives a keep, reprice, repackage or retire verdict with one reason. Box Set Case, Title Trend, Backlist against Frontlist and Next Book Forecast (Base, Best and Worst) cover the other weekly questions.

18 calculators, 12 printable sheets, 12 documents, 12 checklists and 34 ready text messages to the assistant, designers, formatter, narrator, ad specialist, accountant and rights agent. This is part six of the Author and Self-Publisher Business suite. A standard .xlsx workbook with no macros and no subscription, with a demo copy full of sample data. Figures are estimates until the stores pay, every target is your own number and nothing here promises sales.

Verdict: {col:bundles.verdict}. Decide by {col:bundles.decide_by}. Check each store's current terms for bundle prices and royalty shares.

Production cost {col:ytest.cost}. Royalties of the last 12 months {col:ytest.roy12}. Yearly return {col:ytest.ret} against your own target of {col:ytest.target}. Result: {col:ytest.pass}.
